events.decision: Implemented timeout-aware task execution and validated the bounded project.
decisions: Use subprocess.run with capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout_seconds, and shell=False.
Reject an explicit timeout_seconds value unless it is a finite positive int or float; reject empty argv and an empty executable entry as invalid records.
Decode timeout bytes as UTF-8 with replacement and map missing output to an empty string so every result remains deterministic JSON.
Keep the existing result shape and report-writing behavior; no new status or environment-dependent field was introduced.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Passing the validated timeout to subprocess.run and converting TimeoutExpired to timed_out will satisfy the timeout contract.
status_changes: untested -> confirmed by the supplied timeout unittest and the boundary smoke test

hypotheses.hypothesis: Normalizing str, bytes, and None timeout output will preserve available output without serialization errors.
status_changes: untested -> confirmed by a timeout command that emitted non-UTF-8 bytes

hypotheses.hypothesis: Treating missing timeout as optional while rejecting explicit null, non-positive, non-numeric, non-finite, and empty-command values will keep malformed tasks isolated.
status_changes: untested -> confirmed by direct run_task boundary checks

events.next_action: No further bounded-project action is required; the parent may inspect return.json and perform its acceptance/close step.
observations: The bounded project contains README.md, src/task_runner.py, tests/test_task_runner.py, and tools/official_subprocess_reference.py.
The initial implementation passed capture_output and text to subprocess.run but did not pass timeout_seconds or catch TimeoutExpired.
Baseline unittest execution produced 2 passing tests and a failure because the timeout case was reported as success.
The shell did not provide python on PATH; the bundled workspace Python executable was used for all validation.
After the change, the supplied tests passed and additional boundary checks passed for invalid timeout values, empty argv, bytes-containing timeout output, and shell-literal argv arguments.

operations.result: Established the contract, current implementation, tests, and bounded subprocess reference.
Read-only reference returned the documented timeout, output-type, and shell-semantics claims.
Added timeout validation, TimeoutExpired handling, output normalization, explicit shell=False, and malformed empty-command handling.
Ran supplied unittest suite, direct boundary smoke checks, py_compile, and git diff --check; all final checks passed.

requirements: Read an input JSON object with a tasks array and emit one result per task in input order.
Report success only for exit code 0 before the timeout; report non-zero exits as failed with exit code, stdout, and stderr preserved.
Report timeout expiry as timed_out with no invented exit code and with captured output preserved when available.
Report malformed task records as invalid and continue processing later tasks.
Execute argv command arrays without shell interpretation.
Produce deterministic JSON and exit 0 for a report even when individual tasks fail or time out.
Edit only phase6a/fixture/task-runner and do not commit the parent repository.

research.claim: subprocess.run passes timeout to Popen.communicate and raises TimeoutExpired when the timeout expires.
TimeoutExpired captured output and stderr may be bytes, so the text-facing report must normalize them before JSON serialization.
An argv list is not shell syntax when shell is false.

validation.observation: 2 tests passed; test_timeout_is_reported_without_fake_success failed with success instead of timed_out.
Invalid timeout values, empty argv, non-UTF-8 timeout output, and literal argv arguments behaved as intended.
